full_judgment:
5. Syed Ishtiaq Ahmed with Mr. Md. Asaduzzaman the learned Advocates appearing for the petitioner company submitted that the revenue authority without application of its mind on the provisions of the law as contained in section 46A of the Income Tax Ordinance, 1984 hereinafter referred to as the Ordinance, rejected the application of the petitioner company praying for tax benefit. In elaborating his submissions the learned Advocate taking us through section 46A of the Ordinance submitted that in the explanation given in section 46A(1) it has been clearly mentioned that for purposes of the said section "industrial undertaking" includes "expansion of an existing undertaking" if the expansion unit constitutes identifiable unit for production or operation of similar or others goods or class of goods or service; and that it appears from the audited accounts submitted along with application for tax holiday benefit in prescribed form that till 1995 the assesse petitioner was equipped with the machineries worth of Tk. 3.89 and odd lacs only and that thereafter the expansion was made With machineries imported through letter of credit and by local purchases worth Tk. 3.5 crores and odd and that for the expanded unit further electricity load was required which was given in December, 1995 and these facts have not been denied by the respondents. The learned Advocate further submits that the respondents also did not deny the facts of going into trial operation with the added machineries on 28.1.96 and starting of commercial production on 1.3.96 and admittedly the revenue authority received the application for tax holiday benefit on 14.8.96 and thus it is clear that the application for tax-holiday benefit was made within 180 days from the date of commercial operation i.e. 1.3.1996 and therefore, the rejection of the application on the ground of limitation is not valid. The learned Advocate submits that the revenue authority arrived at such erroneous decision due to non application of their mind on the provisions of section 46A of the Ordinance wherein it has been clearly mentioned that the industrial undertaking includes "expansion of an existing undertaking" and thus the initial commercial production date of the petitioner company with its machineries worth of Tk. 3.89 lac and odd earlier to 1995 is of no consequence as the same relates to the existing undertaking whereas the production date 1.3.96 relates to the commercial production with the added machinery to the existing unit. Therefore the refusal order passed by the revenue authority cannot be maintained and is had in law and the letters issued containing the refusal orders evidenced by Annexure-F and H to the writ petitions are against the provisions of law and therefore those are without lawful and of no legal effect. 

 6. Mr. Dabiruddin Ahmed the learned Deputy Attorney General, submitted that the provisions of section 46A of the Ordinance require that the expansion units should he identifiable unit for production or operation of similar or other goods but there is no material available on record to show that the expansion of the existing undertaking is identifiable separately and such identification is a question of fact to be ascertained on local physical verification. The learned Deputy Attorney General however could not rebut the submissions made by the learned Advocate for the petitioner company on the point of limitation in as much as the limitation of 180 days is also applicable in case of expansion of an existing undertaking. The learned Advocate further submitted that there is also no material available on record to show that the income of the existing unit and that of the added unit were maintained separately to enable to determine the accounts of the assessee company entitling it to get tax holiday benefit and therefore the revenue authority rightly refused the prayer, however the ground mentioned in refusal letter may not be proper. 

 7. We have perused the application, the affidavit in Opposition of the respondent No. 1 the affidavit in reply and the supplementary affidavit filed on behalf of the petitioner company. We have also considered the submission of the learned Advocates of the respective parties. The admitted facts are that the petitioner company earlier went into commercial production with its machineries worth of Tk. 3.8 lac and odd prior 1993 and that the petitioner company expanded its factory with new machineries and equipment’s worth of Tk. 3.5 crores and odd by importation opening L.C. and also by local purchases and that for the expansion of the unit high tension load of electricity was given in December, 1995 and that there is no denial from the respondents to the statement that the petitioner company went into trial operation after expansion of the undertaking on 28.1.96 and thereafter went into commercial operation on 1.3.96 and that the respondents received the application for tax holiday benefit from the petitioner company on 14.8.96. From the above it appears application was made within 180 days of the commercial operation of the expanded unit of the petitioner company and therefore the reasons given for rejection of the petitioners prayer for tax holiday benefit is without any basis in view of the explanation of meaning of undertaking as per section 46A of the Ordinance and it also further shows that the revenue authority did not apply its mind in rejecting the application more so when the law itself has explained that for the purpose of such tax holiday benefits the "industrial undertaking" includes expansion of an existing undertaking. It appears from the Annexure-X to the supplementary affidavit, which is a copy of the application for tax holiday made in prescribed form, that the petitioner company was incorporated on 30.6.82 and the petitioner company was registered with the income tax authority as an assessee and that the amount of investment involved in setting up of the It industrial undertaking after expansion for which tax holiday was prayed for was Tk. 4.92 crores and that the machineries used in the business carried on in Bangladesh by the petitioner company in its existing unit has not been transferred or used in the industrial undertaking for which approval has been sought for and that audited balance sheets for the previous 3 years were enclosed as required which clearly show that the tax holiday benefit sought for relates to the expande unit/undertaking which fact as it appears has not been considered by the revenue authority and thereby the revenue authority has erred in law in rejecting the prayer for tax holiday benefit on the ground of limitation.
